phase7BrowserHarness.runner: approved pinned Playwright-compatible browser runner invoked by Bun
phase7BrowserHarness.networkPolicy: block external network; allow only the local test server
requiredCapabilities: pixel comparison and failure artifact writing
phase7BrowserHarness.passCondition: The browser harness is installed, version-pinned, and runs every manifest scenario. Its absence blocks visual acceptance.

comparison.maskPolicy: No masks for application content. Only the test-run timestamp and browser-owned caret blink may be disabled or normalized before capture.

baselinePolicy: Baselines are version-controlled PNG files created only from an approved deterministic fixture run.
A baseline update requires the Phase 0 change-control record or an approved UI change record that names all affected scenario and viewport pairs.
Failure archives are Git-ignored operational evidence and must be retained for the release review.
Screenshots, DOM captures, and reports must redact API keys, Authorization headers, raw sensitive media, and full model prompts or responses.

fixtureContract.delivery: The UI exposes a test-only deterministic fixture seam selected before application bootstrap. Production builds must not activate a fixture from a URL, local storage, or server response.
dataRequirements: Fixtures use synthetic resource IDs, relative paths, evidence summaries, and generated thumbnail placeholders only.
Fixtures must never invoke real LLM, VLM, external HTTP, or local filesystem scanning.
Each fixture supplies a fixed snapshotRevision, profile revision, task profile revision, event sequence, timestamps, and ordering.
Each fixture supplies enough data to render its declared selectors without a loading race.

semantic-profile-details-review: The four fixed review regions are present in the declared order: structure, content, samples-and-aggregation, evidence-and-unresolved.
The currently displayed snapshotRevision and profile revision are visible before a user reviews claims.
No content-semantic claim may be styled or labelled as a deterministic fact; sample observations and aggregated claims are visibly distinguishable.
UNKNOWN remains visible with its controlled reason and available next action; it cannot be hidden by an empty state.
A failed or partially completed job cannot replace the last complete profile. The UI identifies the active artifact and any prior complete revision.
Reanalyze, cancel, and retry controls appear only when their job state permits the action, but retain their stable selector whenever rendered.
task-driven-dataset-discovery: The workspace has query input, parsed TaskSemanticProfile review, dataset resource scope, Compatibility filter, default sorting explanation, result groups, and selected-result explanation.
Required conditions are visibly distinguished from preferred conditions before matching starts.
Only COMPATIBLE results with a non-null formal suitabilityScore appear in the default-ranked results.
PARTIALLY_COMPATIBLE, INCOMPATIBLE, and UNKNOWN results appear outside the default ranking with their missing requirement, blocking evidence, or missing-evidence explanation.
A compatibility filter changes visibility only; it must not silently recompute, promote, or suppress formal eligibility.
The selected result exposes satisfied requirements, matched preferences, conflicts, UNKNOWNs, evidence references, revisions, rule version, and generated timestamp.

accessibilityRules.rule: Every enabled interactive control in both workflows is reachable by sequential Tab navigation in visible order; no positive tabindex is permitted.
Keyboard focus has a visible 2 CSS pixel or greater outline/indicator with at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors; focus cannot be clipped by a scroll container.
Each fixed review region and major task-discovery workspace region uses a semantic section/landmark with an accessible heading or aria-labelledby reference.
Icon-only and text controls have non-empty accessible names that state their action; test IDs are not an accessible-name substitute.
Job status, reconnect state, and sanitized errors use an appropriate aria-live status or alert region without repeatedly announcing unchanged SSE events.
Each expandable evidence, unresolved item, and result explanation exposes its expanded state via native details/summary or aria-expanded and is operable with Enter and Space.

layoutRules.rule: Relative paths, source references, and revisions wrap at natural break opportunities; they do not cause horizontal page overflow at either fixed viewport. A full value remains available through an accessible title or explicit copy control.
Long evidence summaries and locators wrap or scroll inside their own bounded code/text area. They cannot overlap adjacent claims, controls, or drawer boundaries.

At mobile-390x844, result rows and semantic claim rows reflow to a single-column readable layout. Tables either expose labeled stacked rows or an explicitly scrollable region with the first column/row label preserved.

At both viewports, cancel, retry, reanalyze, parse, run, filters, and result expansion controls remain visible or reachable by ordinary scrolling and have a 44 by 44 CSS pixel minimum hit target when icon-only.
Sample-level observations include their sample reference and are visually differentiated from dataset-level aggregated claims by a persistent label and distinct container treatment.
No required content, focus indicator, live status, error, or action control is clipped, occluded, or positioned outside the viewport without a reachable scroll path.

assertions: Render events 1 through 3, disconnect, reconnect with lastEventId 3, then deliver replayed event 3 and events 4 through 6.
The rendered timeline contains each eventId 1 through 6 exactly once in increasing order.
The final job state, progress, evidence count, and result revision match the no-disconnect fixture with the same event sequence.
A reconnect indicator is announced once for the transition and clears after synchronization.
Render an in-progress match job, disconnect before result event 8, reconnect with lastEventId 7, then replay 7 and deliver 8 through end.
The final ranked and non-ranked result memberships and selected-result explanation equal the no-disconnect fixture.
No duplicate result card, duplicate error, or duplicate evidence item is rendered after replay.
The UI does not expose a stale partial result as completed before the terminal result/end event.
